chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who slandered his wife, and she was mute, he (peace be upon him) said: They are separated.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce if a man accuses his mute wife of adultery?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the khul' or separation (talfiq) is mandatory when a husband performs li'an against his mute wife, as her inability to verbally deny the accusation creates a unique evidentiary impasse. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on protecting the rights of the wife in cases where the standard reciprocal oaths of li'an cannot be fully executed due to physical disability. It underscores the principle that the husband's oath alone is sufficient to dissolve the marriage when the wife's silence is interpreted as a lack of effective counter-testimony.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, and Muhammad Bin Muslim,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who slandered his wife, and she was mute’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There would be separation between them’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “About the case of a man who goes through the process of al-Li‘an (condemnation) against his wife who is speechless, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘They must be separated from each other.”’
